title: fix(i18n): annotate the nine i18n-extract configs' default export to clear TS2883
body:
Fixes #10868

Nine `scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts` files exported an un-annotated `default`, and each one failed a direct type-check with TS2883. All nine now annotate that export with `ObjectStackDefinition` — `defineStack`'s own declared return type, and a public root-entry export — which is exactly what the diagnostic asks for and costs no precision.

## The fork, and why this PR takes the fallback

The triage ruling made repair (2) the card — stop the leak in `packages/spec`'s build so inferred consumer types resolve through stable, public dts entry points instead of hashed chunk paths — with repair (1) as the fallback *if repair (2) measures infeasible or oversized*. It measures infeasible **as scoped**, and the measurement changes what the real producer-side repair is:

1. **tsup gives no control over dts chunk naming or splitting.** `tsup@8.5.1` hard-codes the dts pass's output as `chunkFileNames: '[name]-[hash].d.ts'` in `dist/rollup.js` (`getRollupConfig`); no `dts.*` option and no `manualChunks` seam reaches it. Read out of the installed package, not recalled.

2. **Removing chunking entirely does not fix the class.** Measured, not argued: a real single-entry dts build (root entry alone, so rollup has one input and cannot split) emitted one self-contained 2.77 MB `index.d.ts` with **zero** chunk references. Compiling `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts` against it did not go green — TS2883 turned into TS4082, and an *additional* name leaked that the chunked build had never surfaced:

   ```
   scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts(24,1): error TS4082: Default export of the module has or is using private name 'BaseValidationRuleShape'.
   scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts(24,1): error TS4082: Default export of the module has or is using private name 'StateNodeConfig'.
   ```

   So the hash-named chunk is a **symptom**, not the cause.

3. **The cause is nameability, and the fix for it is a published-surface change.** `FormFieldInput`, `NavigationItemInput` and `StateNodeConfig` are already public — `api-surface/ui.json` and `api-surface/automation.json` record all three — they are just not on the **root** entry, which is where `defineStack` lives. Appending `export type { FormFieldInput, NavigationItemInput, StateNodeConfig };` to the built `dist/index.d.ts` took the same compile from 3 errors to 0 **with the hashed chunks untouched**. A fourth reading is the control: when the repro program incidentally also contained files importing `@objectstack/spec/ui`, the errors vanished by themselves, because the subpath entry that does export those names was then in the program.

That producer repair adds three rows to `api-surface/root.json`, i.e. it alters the published `.d.ts` public surface — this card's explicit stop-and-report. It is filed as #11350 with the measurements and a four-axis recommendation, and **is not attempted here**. This PR is repair (1), on all nine configs (the eight census entries plus `packages/services/service-storage`).

`packages/spec/**` is untouched, so the clause-② path limb does not fire.

## Before / after

Method (the card's, re-measured on `main` @ `8bdd95535`, not on the card's `5886ee6d22`): each package's own `tsconfig.json`, `rootDir` neutralised, `include: ["scripts/**/*"]`, dependency closure built.

| directory | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/platform-objects/scripts` | 1 | 0 |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/scripts` | 3 | 0 |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/scripts` | 3 | 0 |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-security/scripts` | 3 | 0 |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/scripts` | 3 | 0 |
| `packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/scripts` | 3 | 0 |
| `packages/services/service-messaging/scripts` | 3 | 0 |
| `packages/services/service-realtime/scripts` | 3 | 0 |
| `packages/services/service-storage/scripts` | 3 | 0 |

25 TS2883 to 0. Two notes on the card's table: it listed 8 directories and this run finds the defect in all **9** (`service-storage` reproduces identically), and its per-directory counts differ from today's because scoping the program differently changes them — when `src/**/*` is also in the `include`, other files pull `@objectstack/spec/ui` into the program and some of the errors disappear on their own. That sensitivity is itself evidence for the diagnosis in point 3 above.

**Reverse verification**, predicted direction stated first — prediction: reverting the annotation returns TS2883, 3 for `plugin-audit` and 1 for `platform-objects`. Run from the committed state (`git restore --source=HEAD~1`, revert confirmed on disk by grep before compiling): observed exactly 3 and exactly 1, the same three symbols through the same three chunks. Restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, restore confirmed on disk, both back to exit 0.

## Verification

Gate families derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on the actual diff (the script's own change-set derivation, not a hand-built path list). Union re-run at final commit `989f6eb6a`, clean tree; exit codes captured before any pipe.

- `pnpm check:published-files` — OK (69 publishable packages; `scripts/` is outside every `files` whitelist, so this PR changes no published artifact)
- `pnpm check:slot-lookup` — ratchet holds
- `pnpm check:test-source-alias` — OK
- `pnpm check:type-source-resolution` — OK
- `pnpm check:type-check-coverage` — OK, 65/78 packages type-checked, ledger unchanged
- `pnpm check:type-check-debt` — `--re-measure: OK — 33 ledger entries re-measured, 1897 raw tsc errors total, none above its recorded number` (run after `turbo run build` over the whole workspace, as the gate demands). The four surplus notices it prints are pre-existing TEST_DEBT entries in other packages, untouched by this diff; no ledger entry is raised or lowered here.
- `node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` — OK
- `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs` — OK
- `node scripts/docs-audit/check-affected-docs.mjs` — OK
- `pnpm check:i18n` (convention-triggered: edits a file in a package that owns an `i18n-extract.config.ts`) — `OK (9 packages — all bundles in sync, no undeclared authoring keys)`. This is the load-bearing functional check: the extractor imports these nine configs, so it proves the annotation changed nothing about what they produce.
- `pnpm check:nul-bytes` — OK
- `pnpm --filter <each of the nine> run typecheck` — 8 green; `@objectstack/service-storage` declares no `typecheck` script at all (its coverage is ledgered), so the zero-match is named rather than counted as a pass.
- `pnpm --filter <each of the nine> run test` — 239 test files, 4172 tests, all passing.

## Changeset

None, `skip-changeset` label applied. `scripts/` is not in any of these packages' `files` whitelist (`["dist","README.md","CHANGELOG.md"]`, confirmed by `check:published-files`), so no published artifact changes and there is nothing for release notes to compile. Measured rather than assumed: this PR does not touch `packages/spec`'s build, so the emitted `dist` is byte-identical.

## Filed, not fixed here

- #11350 — the producer-side repair: the root entry does not re-export three types its own public API's inferred types mention. Carries all the measurements above plus a four-axis recommendation. That card is not addressed by this PR and remains open.
- #11351 — `[finding]` the eight `UNCHECKED_SOURCE_DEBT` notes still record "3 x TS2883" for directories that now measure 0, and those directories become graduation candidates. Not repaired here: the edit lands in `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`, which widens this PR's gate surface past the card's.
